info.title: Atako API
info.description:
The Atako customer API — manage AI agents, their files, integrations, billing, and your company/team, programmatically.

## Authentication

Every non-public endpoint takes a Bearer token that is either:
- a **programmatic API key** (`aik_…`) — create one at [app.atako.ai](https://app.atako.ai) → Settings → API keys (company-admin only), or
- a **Supabase session JWT** — what the web app itself sends; not practical to obtain outside a browser session.

```bash
curl https://api.atako.ai/agents -H "Authorization: Bearer aik_..."
```

An API key acts as its owning user, within the limits of the key:

- **Scope** — a `read` key can only call GET operations (any other verb: `403 API_KEY_READ_ONLY`); a `write` key can call everything its user can, except the operations below.
- **Forbidden to every key** — billing changes (every non-GET `/subscriptions/*`), minting agent tokens, listing or managing API keys (every `/users/api-keys` operation), deleting the account: `403 API_KEY_FORBIDDEN`. These need a signed-in user in the app.
- **Expiry** — optional (30, 90 or 365 days); an expired key gets `401 API_KEY_EXPIRED`.

Each operation carries `x-atako-api-key: read | write | forbidden` — the minimum key scope it needs, or `forbidden`.

## Live events

`GET /notifications/sse` and `GET /agents/{agentId}/events` are Server-Sent Events streams (`text/event-stream`), authenticated with the same Bearer header — an API key works.

## Uploading a file

Two steps: `POST /client/files/nodes` then `POST /client/files/{nodeId}/upload-url` return a signed storage URL; `PUT` the raw bytes to it, then call `POST /client/files/{nodeId}/complete-upload`. Grant it to an agent with `POST /agents/{agentId}/file-grants`.

## Other Atako HTTP surfaces (not covered by this spec)

- **Atako MCP server** — `POST /mcp` (auth: same Bearer token as above) exposes the same capabilities as Model Context Protocol tools for AI clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT), grouped in toolsets (`/mcp?toolsets=projects,agents`); a `read` key only gets read-only tools. See [docs.atako.ai/developers/mcp/overview](https://docs.atako.ai/developers/mcp/overview).
- **Content API** (`cak_…` key, `/content/*`) — a separate, more restricted key type for headless CMS-style access to blog/news/use-case content. Not documented here.

## Errors

Errors use a JSON envelope: `{ "error": string, "code"?: string }`. `error` is either a short human-readable message or a SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE code, depending on the route — treat it as an opaque string to match against, not a stable enum across the whole API.

## Rate limits

Authenticated routes: 6000 requests/min per user (`authRateLimit`). Public GET routes: 60/min per IP. A handful of sensitive public POST routes (newsletter signup, email-exists, invitation preview) are limited to 10 requests / 15 min per IP.

## Pagination

List endpoints use either simple `limit`/`offset` query params (marketing content — a plain JSON array response, capped at the documented max) or `page`/`limit` (credit transactions). Neither returns a total count today; fetch until a page comes back shorter than `limit`.

get.summary: Questions your agents are waiting on you for, or your settled history
get.description:
Two sorts, never mixed on the same page. The default — `state=open` (or omitted), no `order` — is the queue sorted the way the Floor shows it: priority descending, then kind rank (blocker, guardrail, choice, info), then oldest first; a plain `limit`, `nextCursor` always `null` (AF-52: this order is fixed, never paginated). Any other `state` (`answered`, `expired`, `withdrawn`, `settled`, `all`), or `order=recent` on `open`, switches to the HISTORY sort instead: most recently settled first (answered date if answered, else created date), paginated by the opaque `cursor` — pass back a page's `nextCursor` as the next call's `cursor` until it comes back `null`. `settled` means any of the three non-open states at once (answered, expired or withdrawn) — use it for a history view that must never show a still-open notice; `all` keeps open notices mixed in, for a combined per-person journal.

A company admin may read a colleague's queue/history with `recipientUserId`, or the whole company's, line by line, with `scope=company` (the two are mutually exclusive) — anyone else passing either gets 403, never a silently empty list. Notices past their `expiresAt` flip to `expired` on read, so this list never shows a stale question.

bearerAuth.description: An `aik_…` programmatic API key (app.atako.ai → Settings → API keys) or a Supabase session JWT.

Error.description: Atako's standard error envelope. `error` is either a short human-readable message or a SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE code (routes are inconsistent about which — treat it as an opaque string and match on it exactly if you need to branch on error type). Some routes add extra fields alongside `error` (see the operation's own error responses).

code.description: Present on some routes; a stable machine-readable code duplicating or refining `error`.

LocalizedText.description: A French base value plus optional translations. `fr` is always present; other IETF locale keys are present when translated.

LocalizedStringArray.description: Same shape as LocalizedText, but each locale holds a string array.

ActivitySummary.description: In-memory working/idle snapshot for the agent, or null when nothing is tracked yet.

Agent.description: List-view agent summary, as returned by GET /agents.

lastMessage.description: List-view preview only — content truncated to 280 chars server-side.

AgentDetail.description: Single-agent detail, as returned by GET /agents/{id}.

directModelId.description: Raw model id for a direct-provider (BYOK openai/anthropic) agent; null for an OpenRouter-catalogue agent.

modelName.description: Display name of the agent's OpenRouter-catalogue model (ai_models.name); null for a direct-provider agent (see directModelId) or an agent left on the platform default.

harnessName.description: Display name of the agent's harness (harnesses.name); null when no harness was picked at creation — the runtime `engine` below is then the only harness.

mission.description: The agent's mission (1–3 sentences). Present only when the caller can administer the agent (`canManage`).

systemPrompt.description: The agent's raw instructions. Present only when the caller can administer the agent.

clientContext.description: Per-agent business context. Present only when the caller can administer the agent.

AgentRecord.description: The raw `agents` table row, returned verbatim by POST /agents (201) and POST /agents/{id}/end (200, under `.session`). Every column, including several operational/internal fields not otherwise exposed.

systemPrompt.description: Raw user instructions (no business context appended).

llmKeyId.description: Set for a BYOK agent (company LLM provider key); null for the platform key.

mission.description: The agent's mission in 1–3 sentences, trimmed.

systemPrompt.description: Free-text agent instructions, trimmed. Stored and sent to the orchestrator as-is (no business context appended).

clientContext.description: Free-text per-agent business context, trimmed. Kept in its own column.

modelId.description: Either an `ai_models` UUID (from GET /models or `aiModelId` in GET /models/catalog) or a raw OpenRouter slug (`slug` in GET /models/catalog, e.g. "mistralai/mistral-small"). A slug unknown to the catalog is rejected with 400. Omitted → admin-declared default model. With a direct-provider BYOK key (openai/anthropic), this is instead the provider's own model id.

teamId.description: Assigns the agent to a shared team instead of keeping it personal.

modelConfig.description: Per-task-type model overrides, forwarded to the orchestrator webhook.

engine.description: Defaults to the platform default engine (hermes). `opencode` additionally requires `allowedRepos`.

allowedRepos.description: Repositories (`owner/repo`) the agent may work on. REQUIRED (≥1) for `engine: opencode`, which also requires an active company GitHub connection; ignored by the other engines.

llmKeyId.description: BYOK: id of a company LLM provider key (see docs — BYOK key management is not part of this customer API cut).

available.description: True only when `target` is strictly semver-newer than `current`.

recommendedFor.description: Task types this model is the admin-curated recommendation for (e.g. 'vision', 'low_effort').

name.description: OpenRouter display name, e.g. "Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 4".

providerLabel.description: Human label — the name prefix before ':', else the capitalized provider.

contextLength.description: No provider pricing is exposed to clients: Atako sells inference at its own rate.

isDefault.description: Preselected when the client picks nothing.

aiModelId.description: Catalog row id, present once anyone launched an agent on this model.

lastUsedAt.description: Creation date of the most recent company agent using this model.

Conversation.description: One chat session between the caller and an agent. A user may hold several; see docs/specs/agent-sessions.md.

key.description: Opaque engine-side key of this thread — the bare user id for the historical thread, `chat:<conversationId>` for every session created since. Read-only.

title.description: Derived from the first user message when not set explicitly.

unreadCount.description: Agent messages newer than this session's read cursor.

feedback.description: The caller's thumbs up/down on this agent reply, if any.

ActivityEvent.description: One entry of the live-activity feed (GET /agents/{agentId}/activity).

origin.description: Discriminated on `kind`: 'chat' | 'cron' | 'subagent' | 'system' | 'email' | 'webhook' | 'interagent', each with kind-specific extra fields (conversationKey, cronJobId, subAgentId, threadId, endpointId, contextId, …).

conversationId.description: Chat-origin events only: the session this event belongs to. Absent on agent-wide origins (cron/subagent/system/email/webhook/interagent).

detail.description: Event-type-specific extra data (tool name/args/result previews, token counts, todos, integration call info, error message, …).

FileGrant.description: A client file/folder granted to an agent (GET/POST /agents/{agentId}/file-grants).

node.description: Only present on the list endpoint (joined).

output.description: Execution content (F1.1, agent-cron-channel). Always null on GET /agents/{agentId}/cron-jobs (perf(projects-cron), PLAN-perf.md E3) — read it via GET /agents/{agentId}/cron-jobs/{jobId}/executions/{executionId} instead.

outputPreview.description: Truncated preview of execution content (max 280 chars) for list display only. Not returned on other endpoints.

noChange.description: Monitor-mode run where nothing changed (successful, no output). Never posted to the chat.

CronExecutionOutput.description: One execution's full output, read on demand (perf(projects-cron), PLAN-perf.md E3).

schedule.description: Cron expression (or a deterministic "once at <ts>" one-shot).

repeatTimes.description: Total planned runs reported by the engine; null = infinite or unknown. A success of a job with a finite count is also posted to the owner's conversation.

mode.description: monitor = watch job, silent while nothing changes.

SubAgent.description: Deduplicated by name (case-insensitive) — most recent run per logical sub-agent.

companyWide.description: Native platform capability (e.g. 'projects'): its connection is a company-wide singleton, resolved lazily wherever needed — never manually connected.

defaultGranted.description: Paired with companyWide: every agent of the company holds a virtual full grant on this connection until an explicit grant row (opt-out or adjustment) exists — see IntegrationGrant.isDefault.

nonDeletable.description: The connection can't be disconnected — DELETE /integrations/connections/{id} refuses with connection_not_deletable.

visibility.description: 'company' = shared with the whole company, managed by its admins; 'personal' = visible to, managed and grantable (to their own agents) by its creator only. Another member's personal connections are never returned.

actions.description: List endpoint, custom MCP connections only (providerKey 'mcp', no catalog entry): the active tools, catalog-shaped.

mcp.description: List endpoint, custom MCP connections only.

connection.description: Only present on the list endpoint (joined).

masked.description: List endpoint only: true for another user's PERSONAL connection (an admin viewing a colleague's agent) — no connection name, only `ownerName`. Revocable, not editable.

ownerName.description: Masked rows only: the personal connection owner's first name.

isDefault.description: Present (true) ONLY on a SYNTHETIC row the list endpoint fabricates for a companyWide+defaultGranted connector (e.g. 'projects') when this agent has no explicit integration_grants row yet — it already has full access by default; this row lets the UI show that instead of "no access". `id`/`connectionId` both equal the connection's own id on a synthetic row (no real grant row exists) — DELETE on that id persists an opt-out (a real row with allowedTools:[]) instead of a no-op. Absent (never false) on a real row.

stripeSubscriptionId.description: Company admins only — omitted for members.

stripeCustomerId.description: Company admins only — omitted for members.

stripeScheduleId.description: Company admins only — omitted for members.

hasStripeSubscription.description: Whether a live Stripe subscription backs this row (false for a self-serve trial without card).

hasStripeCustomer.description: Whether the company has a Stripe customer.

pendingActiveAgentsPurchased.description: Target seat count of a scheduled reduction (AF-57), null when none is pending.

pendingReductionEffectiveAt.description: When the pending reduction lands (= currentPeriodEnd at the time it was scheduled).

cancelAt.description: End-of-period cancellation scheduled on Stripe (billing portal): when the service stops. Null when none is scheduled. On a `canceled` subscription: when the service actually stopped.

pendingPaymentActiveAgentsPurchased.description: A licence increase whose prorated invoice awaits payment (3DS, declined card): the seat count once paid. Null when nothing is pending.

pendingPaymentInvoiceUrl.description: The hosted Stripe invoice to pay for `pendingPaymentActiveAgentsPurchased`. Company admins only — omitted for members.

pendingActiveAgentsPurchased.description: Also mirrored at the top level — see CompanySubscription.pendingActiveAgentsPurchased.

trialAllowance.description: Only when `subscription` is null: what activating the self-serve trial now would grant.

consumedThisPeriod.description: Ledger sum of consumption transactions since currentPeriodStart (or the start of the current UTC calendar month).

amount.description: Signed: positive for grant/purchase, negative for consumption.

amountDue.description: Cents still due (what an open invoice shows).

CustomerBillingDetails.description: B2B invoice details held by Stripe — collected at Checkout, edited in the billing portal.

type.description: Stripe tax ID type, e.g. eu_vat, gb_vat, us_ein.

taxLocation.description: `unrecognized_location`: Stripe Tax cannot place the customer — invoices cannot be finalized.

locale.description: Preferred UI/email locale. NULL = no preference recorded yet.

termsVersionId.description: Published terms version in force at acceptance (legal_document_versions).

tourSeenAt.description: Guided tour finished or skipped. NULL = the web app opens it at next load (first login).

storeyToursSeen.description: Storey (`dashboard` | `projects` | `floor` | `context`) → when its guided tour was finished or skipped. A missing storey = its tour opens the first time the user reaches it.

CompanyPermissions.description: The caller's company-scoped capability matrix, computed server-side (`lib/permissions.ts`, documented in `docs/concepts/permissions.md`). Each flag says whether the UI may OFFER a gesture — it never grants one: every route keeps its own guard and answers 403 regardless. Rights that depend on the object rather than on the member are served by the object instead (`canManage` on an agent, `canArchive` on a project, `canEdit` on the org chart).

CompanyMemberRow.description: The raw `company_members` DB row — unlike `CompanyMember` (used by `GET /company/me/members`, which joins in the user's name/email/photo and the team's name), the three mutation endpoints below (`updateMemberRole`, `setMemberAgentPermission`, `setMemberTeam`) return this row as-is, with no join.

FloorTeamLead.description: The team's accountable lead, already resolved through the organisation cascade (explicit lead, else the company's root admin) and named — never the raw lead_user_id/lead_agent_id columns.

lead.description: null only when the company has no admin at all — the one case where the cascade ends on nobody.

leadIsDefault.description: true when the team has no lead of its own and therefore falls back on the company's root manager — the same warning the org chart shows.

clientId.description: Owner — needed client-side to gate the Retry action to the owner.

managerHumanId.description: Unique human holder of the parent teamPositions row of this agent's own position; null when the agent holds 0 or several positions, its position is a root, or its parent is vacant/agent-held.

managerSource.description: Where managerHumanId comes from: an individual override on the agent (own), its team lead or team position (team), or the company root manager as a fallback (company).

engine.description: agents.engine — same value GET /agents serves, added here so the web no longer needs a parallel GET /agents call just for the floor’s harness chip.

positions.description: Every position this member holds (a member may hold several, unlike an agent).

image.description: The member's own photograph (users.photo, a public Supabase Storage URL), or null when they never uploaded one — the client then draws their monogram.

FloorLayout.description: Stored floor arrangement (AF-41). Only what the automatic layout cannot infer: where each team platform sits, and which desk of its own team an occupant stands at. Reconciled at read time — entries whose id is no longer on the floor are stripped from the served document (never from the stored row).

agents.description: id = agentId, slot = desk index inside the pod of ITS OWN team (slot 0 of team A and slot 0 of team B are different desks).

members.description: id = userId, same slot semantics as `agents`.

FloorState.description: GET /floor/state — single-shot aggregated read for the Agent Floor 3D scene. Nothing stored anew: teams/positions and members come from getTeamsByCompanyId/listCompanyMembers, agents from a floor-specific minimal query.

layout.description: null = automatic layout (nobody ever moved anything on this floor).

layoutVersion.description: Optimistic version of the stored layout; null when there is none.

OrgRef.description: A reference to a member of the organisation, whatever its nature. Humans and agents are the same kind of node in this chart.

OrgTeam.description: A team as the hierarchy needs to see it.

lead.description: The EXPLICITLY designated lead, or null — a team with no lead falls back to the company root, and `issues` reports it as `team-lead`.

role.description: The title of the org-chart position held, when there is one.

manager.description: The individual override, or null when the agent simply inherits its team's lead (the ordinary case).

managerUserId.description: A person answers to a person, or to nobody — never to an agent. Null on the root of the chart.

OrgIssue.description: A rule the structure is currently breaking. A CODE, never a sentence: the client translates. `team-lead` — `id` is a team with no designated lead (it falls back to the root: to confirm, not to repair urgently). `agent-manager` — `id` is an agent with no manager at all. `agent-human` — `id` is an agent whose chain never reaches a person.

OrgNode.description: One box of the chart. `id` is a user, agent or team id depending on `kind` — the single exception being the VIRTUAL team `unassigned`, which has no row in the database and gathers the agents that belong to no team. `name` on that node is the literal string `unassigned`: the client names it in its own language.

teamId.description: On a member node: the team it stands in. On a team node: its own id, or null for the virtual `unassigned` group.

memberCount.description: Team nodes only — agents plus humans attached to the team.

OrgChart.description: The whole chart, and the single payload of every /organization operation — reads AND writes. A hierarchy change moves people who were not named in the request, so a write answers with the recomputed chart rather than an acknowledgement: the client never has to make a second call, nor guess. It carries both the derived SHAPE (`tree`) and the raw CHOICES (`teams`/`agents`/`humans`, with their explicit `lead`/`manager`), which is what an editor needs to show what was decided instead of what was inferred from it.

rootHumanId.description: DERIVED, never stored: the oldest `admin` member. Null when the company has no admin at all — the only case where the chart has nothing to hang on.

tree.description: The chart as a forest. `roots` are the people nobody stands above (normally one). `loose` collects what the structure left dangling — a team whose lead is gone stays on the chart, to be repaired rather than to vanish quietly.

canEdit.description: True when the caller is a company admin, i.e. when the write operations below are open to them. Told here so the client never has to deduce a permission from a 403 it provoked.

OrgCandidate.description: Someone an editor may propose as a manager or a team lead. Impossible candidates are listed too, carrying the reason they are blocked — "why is that one greyed out" is a question about the model, and the choice list is where the model must answer it.

blockedReason.description: Null when the candidate can be chosen. A stable CODE, never a sentence: the client translates it.

ProjectSpace.description: A company-owned grouping of projects. A project belongs to 0 or 1 space; deleting a space leaves its projects without one.

position.description: Reserved for a manual order (no UI yet). Spaces list by position, then name.

ProjectStarter.description: The labels a brand-new project starts with, written by the caller in the user's own language: the wiki home page and the board's first columns. Omit it entirely and the API writes its own French defaults (Backlog / À faire / En cours / Revue / Terminé, page « Overview ») — it holds no translations of its own. All-or-nothing on `wikiTitle` and `columns`: a starter carrying only the columns would leave the wiki in the other language. `kind` — not the translated name — stays the stable marker for "done".

wikiContent.description: Markdown body of the home page. Defaults to a skeleton built from the project name.

wikiMessage.description: Message of the page's first revision. Defaults to « Création du wiki ».

ProjectParticipant.description: Somebody on the project — a human or an agent, both held the same way so a card can be assigned to either. `id` is the project_members row id (that is what a card's `assignee` points at), NOT the user/agent id. `kind` is derived from the row (agent_id set ⇒ agent), never stored.

role.description: Free text shown on the card ("Chef de projet"…) — unrelated to platform permissions.

memberRef.description: The user id (human) or agent id — stable across projects, unlike `id`.

photo.description: The person's own profile picture (`users.photo`), null when they have not uploaded one — and always null for an agent, which has no face. Never a stand-in: a participant without a photo is shown by their initials.

ProjectColumn.description: One column of a project's board. Columns belong to the project — Atako imposes no global set of states — so `kind` is how the rest of the interface knows which column means finished without hard-coding a name.

ProjectSummary.description: One row of GET /projects — aggregate counts computed in SQL plus a short participant list for the avatar stack. Carries no cards.

spaceId.description: The project's space (see GET /projects/spaces); null = no space.

space.description: Name of the space (joined from `spaceId`); null = no space.

owner.description: Display name of whoever opened the project; "" once that user is gone.

cards.description: `done` counts cards standing in the column whose `kind` is `done` (never a column name); `blocked` counts cards carrying a blocking reason. Archived cards are excluded.

Project.description: A project and everything on it, in one read. A card has no status — its state IS the column it stands in — and the wiki is a tree of pages, each carrying snapshots of its own past.

spaceId.description: The project's space (see GET /projects/spaces); null = no space.

space.description: Name of the space (joined from `spaceId`); null = no space.

cards.description: Non-archived cards, ordered by column then position, each with its labels, checklist and comments. The embedded comments carry no `id` here (only author/at/text) — the comment operations return the full ProjectCardComment.

wiki.description: Root pages of the wiki, each carrying its own `children` subtree and its `history` (newest revision first).

ProjectCardChecklistItem.description: One line of a card's checklist — the small steps a card is made of, ticked off without splitting it into more cards.

ProjectCardComment.description: A message on a card — where the discussion that led to a decision stays attached to the work it decided. `author` is the display name frozen when the comment was written, so someone leaving the company never empties the thread behind them. `id` is present on everything the card operations return; the copy embedded in GET /projects/{id} carries only author/at/text.

ProjectCard.description: A unit of work on the board. It carries no status field: where the card stands IS its state, so read `column`. `blocked` and `due` are absent rather than null when unset — asking whether a card is blocked is asking for the reason.

assignee.description: A ProjectParticipant id (project_members row) — human or agent, both assignable — or null when nobody has taken the card.

column.description: The column the card stands in: its state.

blocked.description: Why the card cannot move. Absent when it is not blocked — there is no blocked flag, only the reason.

due.description: Absent when the card has no deadline.

comments.description: Oldest first — a discussion is read in the order it was written, not like an inbox.

ProjectColumnOrder.description: The up-to-date contents of one column, so a board can be redrawn after a move without reloading the project. Only the columns the move actually touched are reported — one when the card stayed in place, two when it changed column.

cardIds.description: Live cards, top to bottom. Archived cards are never listed.

ProjectWikiRevision.description: One past state of a page, kept whole rather than as a patch, so reading an old version costs a single read. `sha` is a 7-character fingerprint unique within the page, and `author` is frozen at write time like a card comment's.

sha.description: Short content fingerprint, as Git displays one.

message.description: Why the page was written, in the spirit of a commit message.

content.description: The page's full Markdown at that moment.

ProjectWikiRevisionSummary.description: A revision's metadata, without its text (perf(projects-cron), PLAN-perf.md E3) — what GET /projects/{id} embeds for every page's history, since that single read already returns the whole project and every revision's full Markdown on top of that made it arbitrarily large. `size` is the text's length in characters, computed in SQL so it never travels over the wire; the text itself is a separate, on-demand read (GET /projects/{id}/wiki/{pageId}/revisions/{revisionId}).

sha.description: Short content fingerprint, as Git displays one.

message.description: Why the page was written, in the spirit of a commit message.

size.description: Length of this revision's content, in characters.

ProjectWikiRevisionContent.description: One revision's full text, read on demand (perf(projects-cron), PLAN-perf.md E3).

content.description: The page's full Markdown at that moment.

ProjectWikiNode.description: An entry of the wiki's table of contents: where a page sits, not what it says. `content` appears only when the caller asked for it (`?withContent=true`), and `revisionCount` lets the sidebar show how often a page was rewritten without loading any history.

ProjectWikiPageDetail.description: An open page: its current text, a page of its history (newest first) and its sub-pages as table-of-contents entries. Every wiki write returns this same shape, so an editor never has to re-read the page it just saved.

parentId.description: null for a page sitting at the root of the wiki.

content.description: Always identical to `history[0].content` — the two are written in the same transaction and cannot diverge.

history.description: Newest first, capped by `limit` (50 by default).

historyTotal.description: Revisions the page has in all, beyond the slice returned.

ProjectWikiPage.description: A wiki page the way GET /projects/{id} embeds it — the whole tree in one read, every page with its current text and the SUMMARY of its history (metadata only, no revision text — perf(projects-cron), PLAN-perf.md E3). free.description: When true, this option opens a free-text field and `text` becomes required on respond.

NoticeAnswer.description: The human decision, once made. `respondedByName` is frozen at answer time so the decision stays readable after the account is gone.

NoticeOrigin.description: Where the question came from — the work object that raised it. Declared by the agent when it raises the notice, never guessed server-side. `null` on a notice raised before origins existed.

conversationId.description: The chat session, for `chat` origins only. This is what the session deep link carries.

refId.description: The object id for the five other kinds: email threadId, webhook endpointId, interagent contextId, cronJobId, subAgentId.

label.description: Human-readable name of that object (session title, thread subject, job title). `null` when it has none or has since been deleted — the link still works, it just shows the kind.

kind.description: Blocked / permission asked / arbitration / information. The first three are blocking: the agent waits.

subject.description: Short, stable — the deduplication key is derived from it, together with the origin: the same subject raised from two different sessions is two questions.

settledAt.description: `answeredAt` if answered, else `createdAt` — always set, including on an open notice. The one reliable date to show on a settled notice with no answer (`expired`/`withdrawn`).

NoticeList.description: `nextCursor` is only meaningful on the history sort (a settled `state`, `all`, or `order=recent`) — pass it back as `?cursor=` for the next page. It is always `null` on the default open queue (AF-52): that sort is a plain `limit`, never paginated.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next history page, null once exhausted (or not applicable).

NoticeCount.description: Badge counters. `blocking` is a SUBSET of `open` (everything but `info`), never a separate total.

option.description: The `id` of one of the notice's `options`.

text.description: Required and non-empty when the chosen option has `free: true`; ignored otherwise.
